Natural numbers are [[number]]s used to count discrete objects, like bananas or dogs.

{{Hidden example}}
$0,1,2,3\cdots$
{{End hidden}}

== Formal definition ==

=== Via Von Neumann ordinals ===

Define

$$
0=\varnothing,
$$

then if $n$ is a natural number, the next natural number
$$
n+1=n\cup\{n\}
$$

Concretely,

$$
1=\varnothing \cup \{\varnothing\}=\{0\},\\
2= 1 \cup \{1\}=\{0\} \cup \{1\}=\{0,1\},\\
3= 2 \cup \{2\}=\{0,1\} \cup \{2\}=\{0,1,2\},\\
\cdots \\
n+1=n \cup \{n\}=\{0,1,\cdots,n-1\} \cup \{n\}=\{0,1,\cdots,n\}\\
\Rightarrow \\
\mathbb N
=
\bigcap
\left\{
A \;:\;
\varnothing\in A
\ \land \
\forall x\,(x\in A\Rightarrow x\cup\{x\}\in A)
\right\}.
$$
<ref>{{#cite:Q2418}}</ref>
